items.content: After Nvidia’s board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Appearing on Stephen A. Smith’s radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Huang would “end up on his feet.”“You know the expression, anybody can be replaced,” Trump said, floating Apple’s ex-CEO Tim Cook as a potential CEO candidate.It didn’t take long for Trump to begin softening his approach, making it clear he’d welcome Huang back into the role of CEO even if Nvidia’s own board wasn’t ready to do so. Behind the scenes, the Trump administration was working to grease the landing for Huang’s return. And soon, Nvidia’s board changed its tune: Barely a week after insisting they all agreed to shut the door on Huang’s return, they voted unanimously to reinstate him as CEO, president, and board director.“There’s nothing wrong with a comeback,” Trump said in a celebratory call to CNBC.Trump then posted an image on Truth Social of Huang transposed onto Trump’s own body in the infamous photo of him raising his fist after being shot at a campaign rally. In his raised fist, Huang-on-Trump’s-body is clutching a scarlet bra, holding it high in the air.“There’s nothing wrong with a comeback”Even after a decisive blow to the president’s power as Democrats swept the midterm elections, Trump appears to maintain his position as a corporate kingmaker. Trump said he spoke with Huang the night prior to his reinstatement and had been in communication with the board both “directly and indirectly.” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement that “President Trump was totally involved” in the board’s decision — Trump decided near the end of last week that he wanted to lead efforts to get Huang reappointed, per The New York Times, so he asked Vice President JD Vance to act as a liaison between Huang and Nvidia’s board, providing reassurances that the move wouldn’t pose a security risk. Trump also reportedly dialed into Nvidia’s Sunday night board meeting to make the case for his return. “I made the deal,” he told CNBC on Monday.News of Huang’s reappointment, nearly as dramatic as Sam Altman’s return to his CEO role after being voted out by OpenAI’s board in 2023, was a widespread shock to experts, analysts, and investors, particularly after Nvidia’s board had assured stakeholders on its quarterly earnings call last Tuesday that the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On Monday morning, a surge in NASDAQ-100 futures hit a circuit-breaker limit and caused a halt in trading over the volatility.Trump has meddled in other messy incidents, including by repeatedly — and perhaps illegally — extending the deadline for TikTok to complete its sale to a US entity, and, he admitted on Monday, protecting Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Although he said on CNBC that Musk is “80 percent super genius, 20 percent he has other problems,” Trump said it’s important to protect people like him and Huang. “We have to protect our brilliant people because we don’t have enough.”But the upcoming Democratic-majority Congress could test both Huang and Trump’s influence. As Republicans prepare for an open presidential primary in 2028, at least one potential candidate appears to be breaking with the president in their skepticism of Huang and Nvidia. And Democrats seem eager to probe both Nvidia and the Trump administration.The past couple of weeks have been tumultuous for Nvidia. Huang admitted he had had an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom some US intelligence officers reportedly believed to be a potential Chinese spy. There were nearly immediate reports of an additional affair with a direct report, as well as an alleged third affair with a second employee. Megaspeed has reportedly also been investigated for a broader attempt to illegally funnel advanced Nvidia chips to China. Huang himself has pushed to open up more chip sales to China, and he reportedly lied to the Nvidia board about his infidelity. He’s scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1st.The Nvidia board tried to address concerns about Huang in its announcement Monday, writing that members “received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” It made assurances that the independent investigation it had kicked off about Huang and foreign intelligence would “proceed to conclusion” with Huang’s cooperation.The board also said it had recently formed an entirely new National Security and Export Control Committee “comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks,” which is working with legal counsel and advisers who have national security experience. Nvidia will be hiring for a new C-suite position, the board said: chief compliance officer. The executive will “oversee compliance” across the company and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance committees. “NVIDIA will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries,” the board added.Still, the reaction to Huang’s return reflects how small the chance of Huang’s return seemed before Trump’s efforts. Although Trump had previously cast doubt on multiple reports that Alice Huang was a spy, The New York Times reported on Sunday that she “kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year.” According to the Times, which cited multiple people with knowledge of US intelligence reports, Kang Wei — Alice Huang’s business partner and, by some reports, husband, who reportedly introduced her to the Nvidia CEO — worked with the same Chinese intelligence agency. But on Sunday evening, Trump still argued for Huang’s return and managed to continue flipping Nvidia’s board in his favor after a weekend’s worth of efforts.“[I]ndefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible”If the board maintained any hang-ups about bringing Huang back as CEO, Trump’s power over the executive branch — and the pressure he could exert with it — might have offered a compelling counterargument. The Securities and Exchange Commission had previously opened an investigation into whether Nvidia “misled investors,” according to The Wall Street Journal. But in a post on Truth Social Monday, Trump said that the attorney general “has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.” Reached for comment, the DOJ did not provide an on-the-record response in line with The Verge’s editorial policy.Key Democrats have indicated that both Nvidia and the Trump administration will be under fire when the new Congress is sworn in — and momentum has built behind GPU export controls, which Huang lobbied extensively to loosen. “Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain.” Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) said in a post on X, adding they’d work “on a bipartisan basis to continue advancing policies that stop the flow of our most powerful technology to the Chinese military and other adversaries.” Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) called the board’s decision “indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible” and pledged to investigate “business malfeasance by NVIDIA and corrupt abuse of power by Howard Lutnick and the Department of Commerce.” He called for “traditional Republicans” to join in the effort.“The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company’s board still owe Congress answers about the company’s compliance with U.S. export controls,” Sen. Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, said in a statement. “Jensen Huang’s return only increases the urgency of passing bipartisan export control bills into law and making sure NVIDIA does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk.” Rep. Jamie Raskin, the top Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee, said, “A real Congress will find out” whether Trump and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had any alternative incentives for their role in Nvidia’s dealings. Sen. Mark Warner, the top Democrat on the Intelligence Committee, called Trump’s intervention to bring back Huang “outrageous.” Rep. Joaquin Castro (D-TX), a member of the House Intelligence and Foreign Affairs Committees, which are interviewing Huang next week, said he wants to know how Trump stands to benefit from “personally champion[ing] Huang’s return.”“We need to know why Trump put his thumb on the scale to have Jensen reinstated as CEO”At closed-door hearings next week, Democrats say they intend to press Huang and the administration further, and several accused the administration of corruption. “We need to know why Trump put his thumb on the scale to have Jensen reinstated as CEO and why his administration failed to restrict the PRC’s access to our most sensitive technology,” Rep. Gregory Meeks, the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said in a statement to The Verge. The board’s decision is “outrageous,” said Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), a member of the House Select Committee on China. “We still don’t know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him, and neither the government nor Nvidia’s own board has completed its investigation,” Krishnamoorthi said in a statement, calling for Huang to testify publicly. “Reinstatement is no substitute for accountability,” Rep. Kathy Castor (D-FL), another China Committee member, said in a statement.California Attorney General Rob Bonta also intends to continue an investigation into the company. “The reinstatement of Jensen Huang does not change the fact that the American people deserve to know what happened here — whether Nvidia misled investors and the public,” California Department of Justice spokesperson Elissa Perez said in a statement.Last week, before Huang was reinstated, at least two Republican China hawks opposed the idea. Sen. Josh Hawley (R-MO), a rumored potential presidential candidate, told reporters that he would not like to see Huang return to the top post, but would “defer to the board how they want to run their company. If it were me and a guy who just was caught up in a Chinese honeytrap — I think is the technical term for it — I don’t think that I would impose massive security concerns, not just for the company, but for American national security.”While it was up to the board to decide whether to bring Huang back, Hawley said, “We in Congress ought to be concerned about the American national security implications and I think we should be looking into that.”Huang “has a serious credibility problem”House China Committee Chair John Moolenaar (R-MI) said on stage last week at the Aspen Cyber Summit in Washington, D.C., that Huang “has a serious credibility problem, and I don’t believe he would be as effective now as he was before.” His office did not immediately respond to a request for comment after Huang’s reinstatement.Sitting beside Moolenaar on stage last week, Rep. Greg Stanton (D-AZ) gave his advice to the board: “Don’t do it. Don’t bring it back. And at the very least, slow your roll, because there are so many questions that have to be answered. What else is out there that Jensen Huang has done to put US national security at risk?” Stanton warned that Congress is just beginning to probe what happened here. “There are going to be very serious investigations with very serious ramifications if in fact it is as it seems,” he said. “The company needs to know this ain’t going away for a while. This is a very serious issue.” After news of Huang’s return, Stanton doubled down on calls for investigations.Other Republicans — some of whom are leaving Congress — notably disagreed with Trump’s jubilance for Huang’s return. “It’s inexplicable to me why they want this guy back as CEO,” retiring Rep. Don Bacon (R-NE) told CNBC. “To me it’s a failure of character.” Sen. Pete Ricketts (R-NE) wrote on X that Huang’s “behavior does not support reinstatement,” and said he must still testify before Congress. “It also doesn’t absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips,” he wrote. Senate Intelligence Committee Chair Tom Cotton (R-AR) wrote on X that he’s not done investigating. “The controversy with Nvidia and Megaspeed is just the tip of the iceberg, and it’s not resolved because Jensen Huang has his job back,” he said. “Congress has much to investigate and we will pass overwhelmingly bipartisan chip export-control bills, including my Chip Security Act, one way or the other.”“Congress has much to investigate”Market analysts have been watching and waiting for a Huang comeback since reports that he had assembled a “war room” of allies to help with his possible reinstatement. Not only did Huang cofound one of the world’s most valuable companies and arguably the most important one in the AI boom, but he has personally helped secure hundreds of billions of dollars in infrastructure funding from US financial institutions. Demand for Nvidia chips constantly outpaces supply, and Huang has had the president’s ear for months. Despite all that, though, Huang’s clout seemed like it wouldn’t help him up until the past 24 hours.Lindsey Stewart, director of institutional insights at Morningstar, wrote in a note that although investors may consider this a “good move given his history of value creation at the company,” questions remain about the best way to provide corporate governance and oversight at such an important company.Jacob Bourne, an eMarketer analyst specializing in ad tech and consumer technologies, said in a statement to The Verge that it was difficult to gauge “how much protection Trump’s assurances will ultimately provide Nvidia.” And Heather West, head of Eurasia Group’s geo-technology practice, highlighted the fact that Trump recently met with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum. The timing offers Democrats and China hawks “a great deal to work with in 2027 as they begin scrutiny into the administration, potential corruption, and large tech companies[‘] actions here,” said West.Analysts at Yorkville Ives wrote in a note Monday that they consider Nvidia a $300 stock with Huang and a $225 stock without him, due to his hard-to-replace influence in the sector. They said an interim structure “could not replicate” his supply relationships with TSMC and others, as well as his place in AI industry dealmaking.“This is a board that reversed itself because the alternative, a founder-less Nvidia at the start of the Rubin cycle with a CEO search running into next year, was the bigger risk to shareholders, and it chose to pair the reversal with the governance architecture investors will want to see around him,” the Yorkville Ives analysts wrote.Even Trump admits, though, that a true comeback story can’t be called in a single day. “I’ve seen some pretty good comebacks but I’ll tell you, what you have to have for a comeback, really, is longevity,” he told CNBC. He described the pep talk he gave Huang the night before. “I said, ‘You’ve got to promise me one thing. You’ve got the brain, you’ve got everything going, you’ve got to work hard. And if you work hard nobody can beat you.’”According to Trump, Huang told him, “I’m going to work harder than I’ve ever worked.”

items.titleZh: 特朗普为黄仁勋策划了一场冒险的回归
items.descriptionZh:
这篇报道围绕英伟达CEO黄仁勋因婚外情及涉嫌中国间谍关联而辞职、随后又在特朗普政府推动下迅速复职的事件展开，涉及公司治理、美国国家安全、对华芯片出口管制和国会政治博弈等多重议题。

报道称，黄仁勋承认与英伟达客户Megaspeed前高管Alice Huang存在婚外情；部分美国情报官员据称认为Alice Huang可能是中国间谍。随后又出现他与直接下属及第二名员工存在婚外情的报道。Megaspeed还被调查是否更广泛地非法将英伟达先进芯片输送至中国。黄仁勋本人一直主张扩大对华芯片销售，并被指曾就婚外情向英伟达董事会撒谎。他原定于12月1日赴国会作证。上述指控和调查结论在原文中尚未完成，报道以“据称”“报道称”等方式呈现。

事件时间线显示，英伟达董事会最初接受黄仁勋辞去CEO，并在一周前的季度财报电话会上向利益相关者保证“不打算让黄仁勋复职”。但特朗普公开表态支持黄仁勋回归，称“任何人都可以被替代”，并一度提到苹果前CEO蒂姆·库克作为潜在人选；随后又软化立场，表示即使董事会尚未准备好，他也欢迎黄仁勋回归。据《纽约时报》报道，特朗普在上周末决定推动黄仁勋复职，并要求副总统JD·万斯充当黄仁勋与董事会之间的联络人，向董事会保证复职不会构成安全风险；特朗普还据称拨入英伟达周日晚间董事会会议为其复职游说。最终，董事会在不到一周内改变立场，一致投票恢复黄仁勋CEO、总裁和董事职务。特朗普对CNBC称“我促成了这笔交易”，并在Truth Social发布将黄仁勋面部合成到特朗普遇刺未遂后举拳照片上的图像，图中举起的拳头握着红色胸罩。

英伟达董事会在复职公告中称，成员“收到了美国政府高层的意见，基于这些意见，董事会有信心黄仁勋复职不会构成国家安全风险”。董事会表示，针对黄仁勋与外国情报关联的独立调查将在黄仁勋配合下“进行到底”；同时新设完全由独立董事组成的国家安全与出口控制委员会，负责监督贸易合规和国家安全风险，并与具有国家安全经验的法律顾问和顾问合作。公司还将新设首席合规官一职，负责全公司合规并向提名与公司治理委员会汇报。董事会称英伟达将继续配合政府调查和问询。

市场层面，黄仁勋复职消息令专家、分析师和投资者广泛震惊。周一早间，纳斯达克100期货因波动剧烈触发熔断并暂停交易。Yorkville Ives分析师称，有黄仁勋的英伟达估值可视为300美元/股，没有他则为225美元/股，理由是他与台积电等供应商的供应关系及其在AI行业交易中的不可替代作用；临时管理架构“无法复制”这些关系。该机构还认为，董事会逆转决定是因为在Rubin产品周期起点寻找新CEO并持续到明年的风险更大，因此选择在恢复黄仁勋的同时搭配投资者希望看到的治理架构。Morningstar分析师认为，投资者可能因黄仁勋过往的价值创造而视之为“好举措”，但如此重要公司的治理和监督方式仍存疑问。eMarketer分析师称，难以判断特朗普的保证最终能为英伟达提供多少保护。Eurasia Group专家则指出，特朗普近期在亚太经合组织论坛与中国国家主席习近平会面，这一时点会给民主党人和对华鹰派在2027年审查政府、潜在腐败及大型科技公司行为时提供大量素材。

国会反应强烈分化。参议院多数党领袖舒默称民主党将动用全部权力调查特朗普政府、黄仁勋、其他英伟达高管以及“为经济利益出卖国家安全”的人，并推动两党合作继续限制最强大技术流向中国军队等对手。众议院议长当选人杰弗里斯称董事会决定“不可辩护、不负责任且不可理解”，承诺调查“英伟达的商业不当行为以及霍华德·卢特尼克和商务部的腐败滥用权力”，并呼吁“传统共和党人”加入。参议院银行委员会首席民主党人沃伦称，黄仁勋回归不会改变国会仍要求其回答出口管制合规问题，反而增加通过两党出口管制法案的紧迫性。众议院司法委员会首席民主党人拉斯金、情报委员会首席民主党人沃纳、众议院情报和外交事务委员会成员卡斯特罗、外交事务委员会首席民主党人米克斯、中国问题特别委员会成员克里希纳穆尔蒂和卡斯特等均要求调查或公开作证，追问特朗普为何施压恢复黄仁勋、政府为何未能限制中国获取敏感技术、特朗普个人能从中获得什么利益。加州总检察长邦塔方面也表示将继续调查英伟达是否误导投资者和公众。

共和党内部也有反对声音。参议员霍利称若换成他，不会让一个刚陷入“中国美人计”的人复职并带来重大安全担忧；众议院中国委员会主席穆勒纳尔称黄仁勋“存在严重的可信度问题”，认为他如今不会像以前那样有效；众议员斯坦顿建议董事会“不要这么做”，并警告国会调查才刚刚开始。退休众议员培根称让黄仁勋回归“是品格失败”；参议员里基茨称黄的行为不支持复职，且英伟达仍须就国家安全和“下落不明芯片”作答；参议院情报委员会主席科顿称，英伟达与Megaspeed的争议只是冰山一角，不会因黄仁勋复职而解决，国会将通过压倒性两党芯片出口管制法案，包括其《芯片安全法案》。

报道还提到，特朗普此前曾多次干预TikTok出售期限，并承认保护特斯拉和SpaceX CEO马斯克，称“必须保护我们的杰出人才，因为我们没有足够多”。但即将由民主党占多数的国会可能检验黄仁勋和特朗普的影响力。随着共和党准备2028年公开总统初选，至少一名潜在候选人已对黄仁勋和英伟达表达怀疑；民主党则急于调查英伟达和特朗普政府。特朗普本人对CNBC称，真正的“回归”需要持久性，他前一晚告诉黄仁勋：“你有头脑，你什么都具备，你必须努力工作。如果你努力工作，没人能打败你。”据特朗普转述，黄仁勋回答：“我会比以往任何时候都更努力。”

需要指出的是，原文并未展开GPU架构、制程、算力、能效等核心技术原理和创新点，也没有提供具体芯片性能参数或产品对比数据。其技术影响主要集中在先进AI芯片的供应、对华出口管制、贸易合规和国家安全审查；应用场景则体现为AI基础设施投资、数据中心芯片需求以及美国金融机构对相关基础设施的数百亿美元级融资。整体看，报道的核心不是技术突破，而是英伟达在AI芯片关键地位下，创始人CEO去留如何与公司治理、出口管制和国家安全政治交织。

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is back. What happens next?
items.description:
After the leather-jacketed CEO, president, and co-founder of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, acknowledged an affair with Megaspeed exec Alice Huang, his company initially announced an investigation. However, after The New York Times reported there was evidence of another affair, this time with an Nvidia executive who reported directly to him, a board meeting that night ended with Huang’s resignation, and Nvidia CFO Colette Kress was installed as the new interim CEO.
And then… Huang was back. 
In recent years, Nvidia has become a key part of the Trump administration’s AI push, a central figure in negotiations over potential Chinese access to cutting-edge AI hardware, and a company that has used its now $4 trillion-plus market cap to finance other AI companies. Saying it received input “from senior levels of the United States government,” Nvidia’s board announced his return as CEO on November 23rd, less than two weeks after his resignation.

items.content: I suppose I must issue a hearty congratulations to Jensen Huang. Huang is CEO of Nvidia again, to the surprise of basically everyone except President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance, who made sure it happened.Now, those of us who had some kind of basic education on what a “free market” is might find it objectionable to have the American president strong-arming a major American company. But our billionaire tech overlords care about the “free market” exactly as much as they care about “free speech,” which is to say not at all. Watching Silicon Valley cheer for what is, effectively, a sign of a command economy has certainly been bracing. But then, why would they give a shit? Their only real beliefs are that they should remain rich and above the law. Jensen may not have exchanged emails with Jeffrey Epstein, but he’s squarely at the Epstein table now.The deal was reportedly brokered by Peter Thiel’s very own boyI have argued here, in the past, that the Epstein case laid bare the real politics of the revanchist American right wing: total elite impunity. Well, here it is again! If you are close enough with Trump, it doesn’t matter if you may have jeopardized national security by fucking an alleged Chinese spy. You won’t even be investigated for it before the American president calls in to your board of directors’ meeting to demand you be reinstated. I mean, it is the era of gangster tech regulation — what were any of us expecting? The deal was reportedly brokered by Peter Thiel’s very own boy, Vance.Just so we can be absolutely clear about what transpired at Nvidia, let’s quickly go through the facts as we know them. A Chinese citizen named Alice Huang acquired the company she renamed Megaspeed, the Singaporean data firm at the center of this inquiry, in 2023. At some point, Huang met Huang, and the two were seen together at a dinner that December. From 2024 to 2025, Megaspeed received more than 200 Nvidia shipments.In September 2025, the US government began investigating Megaspeed for possible violations of chip export controls; that October, the State Department told Trump of Jensen Huang’s affair with Alice Huang, who was described as a Chinese intelligence asset. Also in October, The New York Times first reported on Megaspeed’s relationship with Nvidia. In December, Trump — who has a close relationship with Jensen Huang — allowed Nvidia to sell more powerful chips to China. In March 2026, Marco Rubio warned the government about Alice, and Trump nonetheless invited Huang to a visit in China. In October, The New York Times reported on the affair. Shortly after Huang sent a note to Nvidia admitting to it, several other reports of infidelity — this time with Nvidia employees — surfaced. On November 12th, Huang resigned. On November 17th, during the Nvidia earnings call, the board’s chair said that the company “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On November 23rd, Huang was back.This level of open corruption is genuinely impressiveWhat changed between last week and this week? A week was not enough time to truly review all the information on Huang and his paramour, Alice “No Relation” Huang, the international woman of mystery. The explanation seems to be that Nvidia’s board succumbed to a pressure campaign from Huang’s fellow billionaires, and a direct intervention from the president and vice president of the United States of America.Sure, all these CEOs ostensibly wanted Huang back at Nvidia to keep the AI trade going. Still, watching the likes of Epic CEO Tim Sweeney, former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick, investing loudmouth Bill Ackman, and Elon Musk — who actually did appear in the Epstein files, and who seemed to be pretty friendly with Epstein! — pitch a fit last week was instructive. These men worried that they might be punished for wrongdoing, that they did not get big enough to be above the law. They have now been reassured, and I suppose that is what really matters. After all, Trump said on CNBC that he gave Nvidia’s board assurances that Jensen is “absolutely fine.”This level of open corruption is genuinely impressive, and not just because Huang is CEO of Nvidia again. Almost in passing, Trump noted that he had “protected” Musk in his first term from “a certain incident [that] took place, a very tough incident.” In his own inimitable style, Trump told Jim Cramer, “You wouldn’t have Elon if it wasn’t for me.” Surely there is no possible downside when the CEOs of two of the biggest corporations on Earth owe their jobs to Trump personally.Surely there is no possible downside when the CEOs of two of the biggest corporations on Earth owe their jobs to Trump personallyOne thing that has perhaps emboldened this crew is the stance from professional politics-knowers — and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries — that holding members of the Trump administration accountable might be a hindrance to governing. That accountability was part of the reason for the blue wave in November seems to have bypassed these pundits (and the presumptive House majority leader). But then, why should we believe that Democrats will thoroughly investigate this? Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer is claiming to want an investigation, but I am skeptical of how deep that investigation will go as long as Schumer leads it, and only partially because he’s been allied with Silicon Valley for more than a decade. He also has a daughter who works at OpenAI, a company that Nvidia invests in and that is dependent on Nvidia chips. How hard is he really willing to go?Of course, there may be more to this than just pure economic self-interest. In celebrating Huang’s return, Trump posted a remarkable image. It is an altered picture of Trump himself, taken after a failed assassination attempt in 2024. Trump’s head has been replaced with Jensen Huang’s head. The American flag has been replaced with the Nvidia logo. Huang is waving a bright red bra. It seems I owe Sigmund Freud an apology. In the end, these men fear nothing more than losing power for sexual shenanigans — and especially losing power to a woman.Leave aside the national security issues for a minute and focus on the two Nvidia employees. Dating subordinates is a serious conflict of interest; the CEO of Nestle lost his job for just that last year. This is a major violation for CEOs of normal companies, but it is common practice among the sleazeballs of Silicon Valley: Bill Gates is famous for it and it was plainly rampant at Google, a tone set by Sergey Brin himself. I am sure that you will be shocked, shocked to discover that in the wake of MeToo, Brin was among the men who suddenly swung right. I mean, Musk himself announced he was a Republican the day before Business Insider reported that he exposed himself to a flight attendant and paid hush money to cover it up.If you’re rich enough, and connected enough, everything is permittedThe Republican Party has made the abuse of women without consequences one of its main issues; that the lesser violation of sleeping with subordinates would also be something the revanchists would defend seems obvious. That was clear from the botched investigation of the Epstein affair itself, the botched release of the Epstein files, and the assorted confirmation hearings of Pete Hegseth, Brett Kavanaugh, and Todd Blanche. (To say nothing of the Andrew Tate business.) But in all this, let’s not forget that Trump has been accused of sexual misconduct by no fewer than 28 women. So I’m sure it was an affront to all these guys that not only did Huang’s misconduct include a series of affairs, but he was also replaced by Colette Kress, who is known to be a woman.I suppose we might as well pass by the various reports that Huang allegedly terrorized his employees. In light of everything else, this seems minor by comparison.Anyway I had that all in mind when I saw Epic’s Sweeney celebrating the state intrusion into theoretically private companies by posting “Back in Black,” an oblique reference to Huang’s leather jackets that is also from the later, lesser period of AC/DC, after Bon Scott died and AC/DC became an AC/DC tribute band. He also called The New York Times’ reporting into Huang “lies.” Musk continued his streak of Sephiroth posting: “The mistake has been corrected.” Jason Calacanis, the All-In podcast’s village idiot, posted, “GPU Jesus has risen!” along with an openly blasphemous, AI-generated image of Huang as Christ.Best of luck to Joon Kim, the Wachtell Lipton partner and former federal prosecutor who is conducting “a thorough and independent investigation” into Huang’s alleged misconduct on behalf of Nvidia’s board. I assume Kim has, like the rest of us, gotten the message loud and clear: If you’re rich enough, and connected enough, everything is permitted. Or perhaps, more succinctly: lol nothing matters.

items.titleZh: Welcome to elite impunity, Jensen Huang
items.descriptionZh:
在一场被广泛视为美国科技界与政治权力深度交织的风波中，英伟达（Nvidia）首席执行官黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）在因涉嫌与中国情报人员存在不当关系而辞职后，仅隔一周便在美国总统特朗普和副总统万斯的直接干预下重返岗位。这一事件不仅暴露了美国科技巨头与政治权力之间的复杂关系，也引发了对外国势力渗透、出口管制及企业治理的严重关切。

事件的核心围绕一家名为Megaspeed的新加坡数据公司展开。该公司由中国公民Alice Huang于2023年收购并更名，随后与英伟达建立了密切的业务往来。据已知事实梳理，2023年黄仁勋与Alice Huang相识并曾在当年12月的一次晚宴上共同露面。2024年至2025年间，Megaspeed收到了超过200批英伟达的货物。2025年9月，美国政府开始调查Megaspeed可能违反芯片出口管制的行为。同年10月，国务院向特朗普通报了黄仁勋与Alice Huang的私情，并将后者描述为中国情报资产。同月，《纽约时报》首次报道了Megaspeed与英伟达的关系。12月，与黄仁勋关系密切的特朗普允许英伟达向中国出售更强大的芯片。2026年3月，参议员卢比奥就Alice Huang一事向政府发出警告，但特朗普仍邀请黄仁勋访问中国。10月，《纽约时报》报道了这段私情，黄仁勋随后向英伟达发去备忘录承认此事，紧接着又有多起涉及英伟达员工的不忠行为被曝光。11月12日，黄仁勋辞职。11月17日，英伟达董事会主席在财报电话会上表示公司“不打算让黄仁勋重新担任CEO”。然而11月23日，黄仁勋便已官复原职。

这一反转的背后，是英伟达董事会屈服于黄仁勋的亿万富翁盟友发起的压力运动，以及美国总统和副总统的直接干预。特朗普在CNBC上表示，他向英伟达董事会保证黄仁勋“绝对没问题”。硅谷多位知名人物公开庆祝黄仁勋回归，包括Epic CEO Tim Sweeney、前Uber CEO Travis Kalanick、投资人Bill Ackman以及马斯克。值得注意的是，马斯克本人曾出现在爱泼斯坦相关文件中，且与爱泼斯坦关系友好。这些科技领袖的公开支持，被批评者视为精英阶层相互庇护、凌驾于法律之上的又一例证。特朗普本人还在采访中透露，他在第一任期内“保护”了马斯克免受“某个非常棘手的事件”的影响，并称“没有我，就没有马斯克的今天”。

文章对事件背后的政治生态进行了尖锐批评。作者指出，爱泼斯坦案早已揭示了美国右翼的真实政治逻辑：精英阶层享有完全的豁免权。黄仁勋与特朗普关系密切，即便可能因与中国间谍有染而危及国家安全，也未被调查便获复职。报道称，这笔交易由彼得·蒂尔的亲信、副总统万斯从中斡旋。作者还质疑民主党方面是否会真正深入调查此事，指出参议院少数党领袖舒默虽声称希望调查，但其与硅谷结盟十余年，且其女儿在OpenAI工作——而OpenAI正是英伟达投资并依赖其芯片的公司。

除国家安全问题外，文章还聚焦于黄仁勋与下属约会这一严重利益冲突。文章指出，雀巢CEO去年正是因类似行为丢职，但在硅谷，此类行为却司空见惯——比尔·盖茨因此闻名，谷歌内部也普遍存在，由联合创始人谢尔盖·布林带头。文章讽刺地指出，在MeToo运动后，布林等人突然转向右翼，而马斯克在Business Insider曝光其向空乘人员暴露身体并支付封口费的前一天，宣布自己是共和党人。文章认为，共和党已将“无后果地虐待女性”作为其主要议题之一，从爱泼斯坦案的调查处理、文件公布，到多位争议人物的确认听证会，均体现了这一逻辑。特朗普本人被至少28名女性指控性行为不端，而黄仁勋不仅涉及多起婚外情，还被一位女性（Colette Kress）接替，这在批评者看来是对这些男性的冒犯。

文章结尾提到，英伟达董事会聘请了Wachtell Lipton律所合伙人、前联邦检察官Joon Kim对黄仁勋的不当行为进行“彻底且独立的调查”。作者对此表示悲观，认为Kim想必已收到明确信号：只要你足够富有、人脉足够广，一切都被允许。或者更简洁地说：一切都不重要。

items.titleZh: 衡量 LLM 生成的后量子硬件中的验证缺口（Lucid, EYL）
items.descriptionZh:
Lucid Motors与EYL Inc.研究人员发表论文《From FIPS to FPGA with LLM Agents: Measuring What Tests and Reviews Miss in Post-Quantum Cryptographic Hardware》，聚焦LLM智能体参与后量子密码硬件设计时暴露出的验证可信性问题。随着LLM智能体越来越多地生成RTL代码，并同时生成用于验证这些RTL的测试和评审意见，硬件设计流程中出现“自生成证据”闭环：即由同一类模型既产出设计，又产出证明设计正确的材料。论文指出，这种自证式证据难以支撑可信硬件，尤其在后量子密码（PQC）这类对安全性和标准合规性要求极高的场景中，传统测试和评审可能遗漏关键验证缺口。

论文提出一种七阶段、以验证为门控的工作流，将验证检查作为推进设计流程的前置条件，而非事后补充。其核心创新在于系统性地测量LLM生成的后量子密码硬件中，常规测试与评审未能覆盖的问题，并把流程从FIPS标准合规延伸到FPGA实现层面。也就是说，研究不仅关注LLM能否生成可用RTL，更关注如何用可审计、可门控的验证机制识别自生成测试和评审中的盲区。该方法对LLM辅助硬件设计流程具有方法学意义：它提示设计团队不能把LLM生成的测试通过率或评审结论直接当作可信证据，而需要引入独立验证阶段和缺口度量。

从公开摘要看，论文尚未披露具体的面积、频率、功耗、缺陷检出率或与基线流程的量化对比数据，因此其当前贡献主要体现在验证框架和问题定义层面。技术影响方面，该工作面向后量子密码硬件加速、FPGA原型验证和安全芯片设计流程，强调在LLM进入RTL生成与验证环节后，必须重新审视测试覆盖和评审有效性。应用场景包括PQC算法硬件实现、符合FIPS要求的密码模块开发、FPGA安全原型验证，以及LLM辅助芯片设计中的验证质量评估。总体而言，论文提醒业界：LLM可以提升硬件设计与验证效率，但“模型生成设计、模型生成证据”的闭环会削弱可信度，需通过验证门控和独立度量来补齐测试与评审遗漏的缺口。

items.content: The clean energy revolution hinges on electrifying the entire global economy just as power-hungry data centers are surging. It’s a challenge delegates from all over the world had to grapple with during the United Nations climate conference, called COP31, that came to a chaotic and unsatisfying close in Antalya, Turkey, on Sunday.Each year, attendees try to make good on the commitment to stop climate change as part of the 2015 Paris climate accord. Preventing extreme weather from growing more terrifying, coastal communities from flooding, and droughts from wrecking food and water systems requires slashing greenhouse gas emissions. But in order to power homes or cars with solar and wind instead of oil and gas, they need to go electric.“Every climate minister in the world is thinking about this”To that end, one of the most anticipated outcomes of this year’s negotiations was a deal to raise electricity’s share of global energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035, compared to about 20 percent today. That becomes harder to do, however, when data centers are causing electricity demand to skyrocket. That made the rush of new AI data centers a climate issue alongside talks on how to transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy.“Every climate minister in the world is thinking about this, and it will inevitably come up in the discussions. It’s part of the broader energy transformation,” Chris Bowen, Australia’s minister for climate change and energy and the president of COP31 climate negotiations, told Politico in an interview at the start of the COP31 summit.Despite becoming the longest COP yet, with debates lasting two days longer than scheduled, official negotiations fell apart spectacularly. Delegates ultimately failed to garner enough support to pass the “pact” they’d been bargaining on for two weeks. The EU, UK, and several smaller nations most vulnerable to climate change rejected the deal that they saw as too weak. The pact omitted the term “fossil fuels” despite many nations calling for stronger commitments to phase out oil, coal, and gas. And the US, the epicenter of the data center buildout and the biggest climate polluter historically, was a no-show after the pro-fossil-fuel Trump administration pulled the country out of the Paris accord (twice).With official negotiations falling apart, and countries only making voluntary commitments on AI and electrification, some environmental and humanitarian groups called this year “the worst COP” ever.To meet the Paris goals, nations will need to cut their greenhouse gas emissions roughly in half by 2030 before reaching net zero by the middle of the century. Many tech companies made similar commitments in recent years, including Google, Microsoft, and Meta. But thanks to the AI boom, those goals have fallen by the wayside.Meta is “re-evaluating” its timeline to reach net zero emissions as it focuses on AI, the company said in its annual sustainability report on Thursday. Meta reported a 45 percent year-over-year increase in climate pollution. Google’s and Microsoft’s carbon footprints are also growing despite climate commitments the companies have made. Data centers’ electricity consumption is forecast to double by 2030, according to a forecast by the International Energy Agency.RelatedThe global pledge to use AI for climate good is a cruel joke“That is a huge climate risk: rising power demand from data centres is not yet sustainable, and an AI boom cannot be allowed to become a fossil fuel boom,” Bruce Douglas, CEO of the Global Renewables Alliance, tells The Verge in an email. Data centers were “a key topic” at COP31, according to Douglas, whose organization cohosted a panel on the challenges during the event.In the US, the country with the most data centers, power sector emissions could increase 42 percent by 2030 as energy companies build more fossil fuel infrastructure to meet data center electricity demand, according to a recent analysis by the Sierra Club. Already, hyperscale data centers in the US create more climate pollution than the country of Denmark, a separate study by Harvard researchers recently found.To stop data centers from creating more pollution, they would need to be powered by additional new sources of renewable energy, Douglas says. He adds that data centers are currently competing with everyone else for grid connections, finance, and electricity generation capacity — and against arguably more essential tasks like heating and air conditioning, as well as electrifying transportation.Many tech companies match their electricity use with renewable energy purchases. But unless they’re helping to build new sources of green energy to meet their added electricity demand, they might just end up hogging limited renewable energy capacity. And if more fossil fuels make up the difference, then greenhouse gas emissions continue to rise overall.“Should new green electrons be used for air-conditioning, electrification or data centres?”“In many cases, datacentres are outbidding other consumers to get speed to power,” Douglas says. “Should new green electrons be used for air-conditioning, electrification or data centres?”There was some progress. Around 80 nations signed onto a voluntary pledge to increase electricity’s share of energy consumption to 35 percent over the next decade, according to COP31 president Murat Kurum. The list of countries that includes, however, hasn’t been published yet, Carbon Brief reports.Another voluntary pledge to keep AI from derailing climate action by calling on data centers to run on less polluting energy also failed to garner much support. Douglas notes that by using the term “low-emission energy,” the pledge still leaves the door open for natural gas (which produces less carbon pollution than coal when burned but is a significant source of methane pollution) to keep powering data centers.“The Antalya A.I. pledge is a step in the right direction to address an important piece of the impacts, but needs teeth in order to translate into stronger protections for people and the planet,” the nonprofit Natural Resources Defense Council said in a statement when the pledge was first announced. “The speed, scale and scope of this challenge is bigger than perhaps anything before it, and the guardrails must be commensurate.”

items.titleZh: 人工智能数据中心给混乱的联合国气候谈判再添变数
items.descriptionZh:
在土耳其安塔利亚举行的联合国气候大会COP31在混乱和不满中落幕。此次会议的核心背景是：全球清洁能源转型要求把家庭、交通等各部门全面电气化，而与此同时，高耗能的AI数据中心正在推动电力需求激增，使AI基础设施成为气候谈判无法回避的议题。各国代表原本希望延续2015年《巴黎协定》的承诺，通过削减温室气体排放，避免极端天气、海平面上升和干旱对粮食与水系统造成更严重冲击。要实现以太阳能、风能替代石油和天然气为住宅和汽车供能，全球必须加快电气化进程。因此，本届谈判最受期待的成果之一，是到2035年将电力在全球能源消费中的占比从目前约20%提高到35%。但AI数据中心的快速扩张使这一目标更难实现。

澳大利亚气候变化与能源部长、COP31谈判主席克里斯·鲍文在峰会开始时表示，全球每位气候部长都在思考这一问题，它必然进入讨论，是更广泛能源转型的一部分。尽管COP31成为历时最长的一届气候大会，辩论比原计划多出两天，但官方谈判最终破裂。代表们未能为谈判两周的“协议”争取到足够支持。欧盟、英国以及一些最易受气候变化影响的小国认为协议过弱而拒绝接受。协议文本未写入“化石燃料”一词，尽管许多国家呼吁作出更强承诺，逐步淘汰石油、煤炭和天然气。美国作为数据中心建设中心和历史上最大气候污染国，在支持化石燃料的特朗普政府再次退出《巴黎协定》后缺席会议。由于官方谈判破裂，各国仅在AI和电气化方面作出自愿承诺，一些环保和人道主义组织称今年是“最糟糕的COP”。

要兑现巴黎目标，各国需在2030年前将温室气体排放大致减半，并在本世纪中叶实现净零。谷歌、微软和Meta等科技公司近年也作出类似承诺，但AI热潮使这些目标被搁置。Meta在年度可持续报告中表示，随着公司聚焦AI，正在“重新评估”实现净零排放的时间表；其气候污染同比增加45%。谷歌和微软的碳足迹也在增长。国际能源署预测，到2030年数据中心用电量将翻倍。全球可再生能源联盟首席执行官布鲁斯·道格拉斯警告，数据中心电力需求上升尚不可持续，AI热潮不能被允许变成化石燃料热潮。数据中心是COP31的“关键议题”之一，该组织还联合主办了相关小组讨论。

在美国这个数据中心最多的国家，塞拉俱乐部近期分析认为，随着能源公司为满足数据中心用电需求建设更多化石燃料基础设施，到2030年电力部门排放可能增加42%。哈佛研究人员的另一项研究还发现，美国超大规模数据中心造成的气候污染已超过丹麦全国。道格拉斯指出，要避免数据中心制造更多污染，必须由新增可再生能源为其供电。目前数据中心正在与其他用户竞争电网接入、融资和发电能力，并与供暖空调、交通电气化等可能更基本的任务争夺资源。许多科技公司通过购买可再生能源来匹配用电，但除非它们帮助建设新增绿色能源以满足额外需求，否则可能只是占用有限的清洁电力容量；若缺口由更多化石燃料填补，总体温室气体排放仍会上升。道格拉斯质疑，新增的绿色电力究竟应优先用于空调、电气化还是数据中心，并指出数据中心在许多情况下正以更高出价换取快速供电。

会议也取得一些有限进展。COP31主席穆拉特·库鲁姆称，约80个国家签署自愿承诺，计划在未来十年将电力在能源消费中的占比提高到35%，但据Carbon Brief报道，签署国名单尚未公布。另一项旨在防止AI破坏气候行动的自愿承诺，呼吁数据中心使用污染更低的能源，但未获得广泛支持。道格拉斯指出，该承诺使用“低排放能源”的措辞，仍为天然气继续为数据中心供电留下空间；天然气燃烧时碳排放低于煤炭，但仍是重要甲烷污染来源。非营利组织自然资源保护委员会在承诺首次公布时表示，安塔利亚AI承诺是应对部分影响的正确方向，但需要“牙齿”才能转化为对人和地球更强保护；这一挑战的速度、规模和范围可能超过以往任何问题，护栏必须与之相称。

总体来看，COP31凸显了AI算力扩张与全球气候目标之间的结构性冲突：AI模型训练和推理需要大规模GPU集群和超大规模数据中心，带来持续攀升的电力与冷却需求；在电网扩容和清洁能源建设跟不上时，新增负荷可能延长化石燃料基础设施寿命，推高电力部门排放。技术影响和应用场景不仅涉及AI产业竞争力，也涉及电网规划、可再生能源投资、数据中心选址与能效、企业净零承诺可信度，以及气候政策如何为数据中心设定“额外新增清洁电力”和排放约束。若缺乏有约束力的政策与新增清洁电源，AI繁荣可能削弱电气化减排效果，并挤占其他民生和交通电气化所需的有限绿色电力。

items.content: The Jensen Huang era of Nvidia nearly came to an end this month. Huang, who three decades ago cofounded what’s come to be considered one of the most important companies in AI, resigned from his role on November 12th over mounting scrutiny around his alleged affairs. Huang admitted he had been “unfaithful” to his wife and that he “created problems for the board.”Huang’s resignation came after weeks of escalating problems, both personal and professional. First, reporting from The New York Times said he had a “close relationship” with a woman passing intelligence to China. Subsequent reporting said that China’s intelligence agency had enlisted that woman — Alice Huang, then an executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed — to spy on Nvidia’s leader, and that the Singapore-based company was under investigation for potentially smuggling AI chips to China. Stories followed that indicated Huang was having an affair with Alice as well as an Nvidia executive, vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell.So when Huang resigned less than two weeks ago, the decision seemed final. Even Nvidia’s board appeared unwilling to budge. “The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” board chair Harvey Jones said during an earnings call last week.But in the days following Huang’s resignation, the founder’s allies — including President Donald Trump — mounted a pressure campaign that brought him back to the company he created and sent Nvidia’s share price rocketing upward, almost as though he had never left.The campaign in support of Huang began almost immediately after his resignation. A coterie of tech leaders began posting in support of Nvidia’s founder: Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney questioned the motives of journalists who broke the stories about his affairs. Tesla CEO Elon Musk likened Huang’s departure to “kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak.” OpenAI CEO Sam Altman later said on stage, “It’s hard to imagine the AI revolution without Jensen.”“If I didn’t get involved, you’d probably have a very sad Nvidia for a long time to come.”— Donald TrumpMeanwhile, some of those tech leaders began questioning aspects of the reporting that led to Huang’s exit. Venture capitalist and former White House AI czar David Sacks cast doubt that Alice Huang was a spy, citing a lack of confirmation from US officials. Trump exacerbated the uncertainty, telling reporters, “I don’t know that she is a spy,” despite reports saying the assessment had relied on US intelligence sources.Nvidia’s board, meanwhile, found itself in a tough position. The company’s shares crashed following Huang’s departure, and they didn’t pick up even after a rosy earnings report. The board was also scrambling to find a new CEO, something industry analysts speculated would prove exceptionally difficult. Reports indicated that Nvidia was considering hiring Arm CEO Rene Haas and Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji, both of whom already have powerful roles in the chip industry.Trump quickly warmed up to Huang’s return, too. The president — whose investment accounts traded up to $97 million worth of Nvidia stock since returning to office — initially floated the idea of having former Apple CEO Tim Cook take Huang’s place, before saying that it “certainly isn’t a bad idea” to bring Huang back.This past weekend, Trump appears to have inserted himself into the situation directly. A report from The New York Times says that Trump asked Vice President JD Vance to work with Huang and Nvidia’s board to “resolve the situation,” while the Trump administration reassured the board that it “did not believe that Mr. Huang himself posed a national security risk.” Semafor reports that Trump even called in to Nvidia’s board meeting to advocate for Huang’s reinstatement. Sunday evening, Trump said in a post on Truth Social that he hopes Nvidia’s board “rehires Jensen Huang.”Hours later, Nvidia’s board did just that. The board announced on Monday that it reinstated Huang as its CEO, president, and board member. In its statement, the board said that it received input “from senior levels of the United States government,” and determined that “Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.”Trump immediately took credit for Huang’s reinstatement, with White House spokesperson Steven Cheung saying the president “was totally involved” in the decision. “If I didn’t get involved, you’d probably have a very sad Nvidia for a long time to come,” Trump said during an interview with CNBC. He added in a post on Truth Social that the US attorney general confirmed that it doesn’t have evidence that Huang “engaged in any unlawful conduct.”RelatedWhite House brags that Trump was ‘totally involved’ in getting Jensen reinstatedTech leaders are celebrating Jensen Huang’s returnNvidia’s shares rose on the news of Huang’s reinstatement, while tech leaders celebrated his return on social media. But the saga is likely far from over. The board said it will finish its investigation into Huang, the Securities and Exchange Commission is looking into Nvidia’s “accounting practices,” and Megaspeed is being investigated by the Justice Department. Even Trump has said that Nvidia should continue its internal investigation about export controls compliance.Trump’s apparent involvement also leaves plenty of room for scrutiny from Democratic lawmakers, who will control the House and Senate next year. Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) called Nvidia’s decision “reckless” and urged the Trump administration to explain the “input” government officials provided to the company’s board.Huang’s stunning reinstatement still leaves many questions unanswered. Even though the backing of Wall Street, the White House, and Silicon Valley may have brought Huang back as CEO, a new wave of scrutiny from federal regulators and lawmakers is just getting started.

items.titleZh: 黄仁勋如何再次成为英伟达CEO
items.descriptionZh:
英伟达（Nvidia）联合创始人兼CEO黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）经历了一场近乎“去职又复职”的公司治理与政治风波。报道显示，黄仁勋在11月12日辞去CEO职务，原因是围绕其个人关系与公司外部风险的审查不断升级。他承认对妻子“不忠”，并称自己“给董事会制造了问题”。此前《纽约时报》报道称，他与一名向中国传递情报的女性保持“密切关系”；后续报道称，中国情报机构招募了这名女性——当时在英伟达客户Megaspeed任职的Alice Huang——以刺探英伟达领导人，而总部位于新加坡的Megaspeed正因可能向中国走私AI芯片而接受调查。还有报道称，黄仁勋与Alice Huang以及英伟达医疗健康业务副总裁Kimberly Powell存在婚外情。英伟达董事会一度态度坚决，董事会主席Harvey Jones在财报电话会上称，董事会“一致接受其辞职，不打算让Jensen重新担任CEO”。

黄仁勋辞职后，英伟达股价大跌，即便发布乐观财报也未能提振。董事会还面临寻找新CEO的难题，业内分析认为接任者极难寻找，报道称英伟达曾考虑Arm CEO Rene Haas和苹果硬件负责人Johny Srouji。与此同时，黄仁勋的支持者迅速展开施压行动，包括美国总统特朗普。Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney质疑相关报道记者的动机；特斯拉CEO马斯克将黄仁勋离职比作“在连胜时把迈克尔·乔丹踢出球队”；OpenAI CEO Sam Altman称“很难想象没有Jensen的AI革命”。部分科技领袖还质疑有关Alice Huang是间谍的报道，风险投资人、前白宫AI事务负责人David Sacks称缺乏美国官员确认；特朗普也对记者表示“我不知道她是不是间谍”，尽管报道称相关评估依赖美国情报来源。

政治层面的介入进一步升级。报道称，特朗普自重返白宫以来，其投资账户交易了最高价值9700万美元的英伟达股票；他最初提出让前苹果CEO Tim Cook接替黄仁勋，随后又称让黄仁勋回归“当然不是坏主意”。上周末，特朗普被指要求副总统JD Vance与黄仁勋及英伟达董事会合作“解决局面”，特朗普政府还向董事会保证“不认为黄仁勋本人构成国家安全风险”。Semafor报道称，特朗普甚至打电话参加英伟达董事会会议，主张让黄仁勋复职。周日晚，特朗普在Truth Social发文称，希望英伟达董事会“重新聘用Jensen Huang”。数小时后，英伟达董事会于周一宣布恢复黄仁勋的CEO、总裁及董事会成员职务。董事会在声明中称，其收到“美国政府高层”的意见，并认定“黄仁勋复职不构成国家安全风险”。特朗普随即邀功，白宫发言人Steven Cheung称总统“完全参与”了该决定；特朗普在接受CNBC采访时称，“如果我没有介入，英伟达可能会在很长一段时间里非常惨”，并称美国司法部长确认没有证据表明黄仁勋“从事任何违法行为”。

黄仁勋复职消息推动英伟达股价上涨，科技领袖也在社交媒体上庆祝。但事件远未结束：董事会称将完成对黄仁勋的调查，美国证券交易委员会正在审查英伟达的“会计实践”，Megaspeed正接受司法部调查，特朗普也表示英伟达应继续就出口管制合规进行内部调查。特朗普的明显介入还可能招致民主党议员的审查，后者将在明年控制参众两院。参议员Elizabeth Warren称英伟达的决定“鲁莽”，并要求特朗普政府解释官员向公司董事会提供了何种“意见”。总体看，华尔街、白宫和硅谷的支持虽让黄仁勋重回CEO之位，但联邦监管机构与国会议员的新一轮审查才刚刚开始，许多问题仍未得到回答。原文未涉及具体芯片架构、技术原理或性能参数，因此无法展开技术对比；但其核心影响在于，英伟达作为AI芯片关键供应商，其领导层动荡、出口管制合规与地缘政治风险会直接影响投资者信心、AI供应链稳定以及美国对华芯片管制政策的外部审视。

items.title: Penguin shows off photonic memory box at SC26 that can expand AI accelerator capacity over optical links
items.description: Penguin Solutions demonstrates external memory box with up to 576 GB of HBM3E and 16 TB of DDR5 inside that connects to hosts using optical links. There is a major caveat with this one as it does not seem to support existing servers and accelerators.
items.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Instagram Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Penguin Solutions showed off its MemoryAI Photonic Appliance remote memory system at Supercomputer 2026 (SC26), with customer samples scheduled for the second half of 2027. The device supports up to 576 GB of HBM3E with an aggregate bandwidth of up to 7.2 TB/s, and connects to systems using optical interconnects via the CXL.mem 3.1 protocol. HBM memory capacity is usually one of the major bottlenecks of contemporary AI accelerators, which is why, when developers face it, they tend to add or upgrade their accelerators. Penguin Solutions' new device aims to solve that, but there are drawbacks.The MemoryAI Photonic Appliance is designed to accommodate up to 576 GB of HBM3E and 16 TB of DDR5 memory, with overall bandwidth targeting 7.2 TB/s. The external memory box supports three memory access configurations: HBM Direct Mode, HBM-DDR5 Cached Mode, and DDR5 Direct Mode. The first provides access to external HBM3E, the second combines HBM3E and DDR5 in a tiered memory sub-system with HBM3E acting like a write-through cache for DDR5, while the third provides access to DDR5 without an intermediate HBM cache. Meanwhile, hardware semaphores (HSEMs) enable software-managed memory consistency across multiple host processors (i.e., if more than one host processor accesses the same memory location, software can use semaphores to ensure that only one host processor can modify data). (Image credit: Marvell)The Penguin appliance relies on Marvell's architecture that consists of Photonic Fabric Memory Modules (PFMMs) and Photonic Fabric network interface cards (PF-NICs). The device uses eight PFMM modules; each integrates a memory controller, eight DDR5 DIMM interfaces, 72 GB of HBM3E cache, and a photonic interposer with 16 transmit and 16 receive channels operating at 224 Gbps. This provides approximately 7.2 Tbps of aggregate bidirectional optical bandwidth per module, or 57.6 Tbps (7.2 TB/s) for the entire appliance, equivalent to approximately 3.6 TB/s in each direction.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: (Image credit: Marvell)Marvell offers two ways to connect processors to the external memory pool. The first uses a Photonic Fabric network interface card (PF-NIC) with PCIe 6.0 and CXL 3.1 connectivity, which provides up to 2 Tbps of bandwidth and memory access latency below 350ns, excluding PCIe/CXL overhead. The second relies on a Photonic Fabric chiplet integrated into an XPU, which offers up to 14.4 Tbps of bandwidth and latency below 200ns. Both approaches enable processors to access shared memory over optical links across distances of up to 30 meters. Meanwhile, the chiplet approach requires accelerator designers to install the chiplet, while transparent memory expansion using the PF-NIC requires the host to support its memory mapping at both the hardware and software levels.Marvell's architecture is designed to enable compatible host systems to access external memory through ordinary load/store memory operations rather than RDMA data transfers, but this requires specific hardware capabilities on the host side. Most modern CPUs support PCIe as well as the CXL.mem protocol for memory expansion. However, the situation is different for AI GPUs. You may like Hot Chips 2026: d-Matrix stacks AI accelerator directly on custom DRAM for 100 TB/s per card Hot Chips 2026: High Bandwidth Flash promises massive bandwidth and capacity, but its usability is extremely limited AMD shares how it can retain 95% of server performance with just half the DRAM, sidestepping memory shortages with MEXT Nvidia's data center GPUs support PCIe, NVLink, and various memory management mechanisms, but they do not support a general-purpose CXL.mem host interface for memory expansion. Similarly, AMD's Instinct accelerators use PCIe and Infinity Fabric for connectivity, but they do not generally support CXL.mem. In theory, accelerators without native CXL.mem support could theoretically access the appliance through a CXL-capable CPU, provided their coherent interconnect supports access to CXL-attached memory. However, this would introduce additional latency, which will extend well beyond the advertised sub-350ns figure (which already excludes PCIe/CXL overhead), which could greatly reduce the actual performance benefits provided by extra capacity.As a result, PFMMs and Penguin's MemoryAI Photonic Appliance can extend usable memory capacity only for select host systems without major performance penalties. These could include custom XPUs equipped with Marvell's Photonic Fabric chiplets, CPUs or other PUs that support CXL.mem and PF-NIC with memory mapping mechanism, and potentially future AI accelerators that support CXL.mem or integrate Marvell's Photonic Fabric. Obviously, this means that such systems will get an indisputable advantage over machines based on conventional accelerators from AMD and Nvidia in the form of memory upgrades.Speaking of advantages, we must note that while an aggregate bi-directional bandwidth target of 7.2 TB/s (3.6 TB/s in both directions) seems formidable (it is only a bit lower than memory bandwidth of B300 SXM that comes at 7.7 TB/s), it is set to be shared between multiple accelerators (eight accelerators in a hypothetical scenario), which will provide limited bandwidth to each one. Although Penguin promises transparent access to external memory without modifications to applications, the appliance will require compatible memory management software (in addition to host hardware), which will treat external memory as another memory tier. While extra memory is always welcome, performance benefits of complex multi-tier memory subsystems depend heavily on workloads and efficient data placement. Consequently, the appliance's practical advantages remain to be demonstrated.Penguin showcased the appliance this week; however, customer samples are scheduled for the second half of 2027, which likely means that the device and/or underlying hardware, firmware, and software need polishing. That said, practical performance and economic advantages of Penguin's MemoryAI Photonic Appliance remain to be seen when everything works as intended. In any case, do not expect deployments of such systems before 2028. This begs the question of where Penguin Solutions plans to source HBM3E in volume in 2028, when the industry will have transitioned to HBM4 and will be in the midst of transition to HBM4E.

items.titleZh: Penguin在SC26上展示光子内存盒，可通过光链路扩展AI加速器容量
items.descriptionZh:
在SC26上，Penguin Solutions展示了MemoryAI Photonic Appliance远程内存系统，计划于2027年下半年向客户提供样品。该设备面向当前AI加速器最突出的瓶颈之一——HBM容量不足：当模型、KV缓存或训练状态超出单卡HBM容量时，开发者往往只能增加或升级加速器。Penguin试图通过外置、光互连的HBM/DDR5内存池扩展可用内存容量，而不是直接更换加速器。

从架构看，该设备最多支持576 GB HBM3E和16 TB DDR5，整体带宽目标为7.2 TB/s，并通过光互连和CXL.mem 3.1协议连接主机系统。它提供三种内存访问模式：HBM Direct模式直接访问外置HBM3E；HBM-DDR5 Cached模式把HBM3E作为DDR5的写通缓存，形成分级内存子系统；DDR5 Direct模式则不经HBM缓存直接访问DDR5。设备还集成硬件信号量（HSEM），用于多主机处理器场景下的软件管理内存一致性，确保多个主机访问同一内存位置时只有一个主机能修改数据。

该产品基于Marvell的Photonic Fabric架构，由Photonic Fabric Memory Modules（PFMM）和Photonic Fabric网卡（PF-NIC）组成。整机使用8个PFMM，每个模块集成内存控制器、8个DDR5 DIMM接口、72 GB HBM3E缓存，以及一个光子中介层，包含16个发送和16个接收通道，每通道224 Gbps。由此每个模块提供约7.2 Tbps双向光带宽，整机合计57.6 Tbps，即7.2 TB/s，约合每个方向3.6 TB/s。Marvell提供两种主机连接方式：一是PCIe 6.0和CXL 3.1的PF-NIC，最高2 Tbps带宽，内存访问延迟低于350 ns（不含PCIe/CXL开销）；二是集成到XPU中的Photonic Fabric小芯片，最高14.4 Tbps带宽，延迟低于200 ns。两种方式都可通过最长30米的光链路让处理器访问共享内存。区别在于，小芯片方案需要加速器设计者集成该小芯片；PF-NIC的透明内存扩展则要求主机在硬件和软件层面支持其内存映射。

技术原理上，Marvell架构希望让兼容主机通过普通load/store内存操作访问外置内存，而不是通过RDMA式数据传输。这能降低编程模型复杂度，但依赖主机侧特定硬件能力。多数现代CPU支持PCIe和CXL.mem内存扩展，AI GPU的情况则不同：Nvidia数据中心GPU支持PCIe、NVLink及多种内存管理机制，但不支持用于内存扩展的通用CXL.mem主机接口；AMD Instinct加速器使用PCIe和Infinity Fabric连接，一般也不支持CXL.mem。理论上，缺少原生CXL.mem支持的加速器可通过支持CXL的CPU访问该设备，前提是其一致性互连支持访问CXL附加内存，但这会引入额外延迟，远高于宣传的低于350 ns水平（该数字本身已排除PCIe/CXL开销），可能大幅削弱增加容量带来的实际性能收益。

因此，PFMM和MemoryAI Photonic Appliance目前只能为特定主机系统扩展可用内存而不造成重大性能损失，包括配备Marvell Photonic Fabric小芯片的定制XPU、支持CXL.mem和PF-NIC内存映射机制的CPU或其他处理单元，以及未来支持CXL.mem或集成Marvell光子架构的AI加速器。这意味着这类系统可能相对基于AMD、Nvidia常规加速器的机器获得内存升级优势，但生态覆盖面有限。

性能对比方面，7.2 TB/s双向总带宽（每方向3.6 TB/s）看似可观，仅略低于Nvidia B300 SXM的7.7 TB/s内存带宽，但它是整机共享带宽。若按假设场景连接8个加速器，平均每个加速器分到的带宽有限，还会受到单卡PF-NIC最高2 Tbps等上限约束。Penguin宣称可透明访问外置内存、无需修改应用，但实际需要兼容的内存管理软件，把外置内存视为新的内存层级；复杂多级内存子系统的性能收益高度依赖工作负载和高效数据放置，实际优势仍有待验证。

应用场景上，这类光互连远程内存池适合内存容量受限的AI训练和推理、KV缓存扩展、检查点与优化器状态存放、内存数据库、图分析以及多加速器共享内存池等场景；30米光链路也使其可用于机架内或跨机架的内存解耦。其影响在于，若主机生态支持到位，可能推动AI系统从“单卡HBM容量决定上限”转向“光互连共享HBM/DDR5内存池”，为定制XPU和CXL服务器架构提供差异化优势。但风险同样明显：客户样品要到2027年下半年，实际部署预计不早于2028年；届时行业已转向HBM4并处于向HBM4E过渡阶段，Penguin如何大批量采购HBM3E、以及硬件、固件和软件能否成熟到兑现性能与经济性，仍是待解问题。

items.content: It sure looked like President Donald Trump played a role in Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia CEO — and now the White House is making sure everyone knows he was. “President Trump was totally involved and this is a great decision by the NVIDIA board,” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement, which was first reported by Semafor. “We have to protect our geniuses.”Trump later went on CNBC with a similar statement. “We have to protect our geniuses,” he said on the air. Trump said he “believed very strongly” that Huang should be reinstated. “We’ve done a very thorough investigation, and the investigation showed that he did — I mean, he had bad judgment having to do with somewhat unrelated incidents. But he did nothing wrong.”Trump also said, “If I didn’t get involved, you’d probably have a very sad Nvidia for a long time to come.”Nvidia said in its announcement that its board “received input from senior levels of the United States government” that made them confident reinstating Huang would not pose a national security risk, following reports about his involvement with an alleged Chinese spy.Trump also posted on Truth Social that Nvidia’s board “made the correct and proper decision” to reinstate Huang, adding:“The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.”Less than 12 hours earlier, Trump said in a separate post that Huang’s reinstatement “would be the best thing” for Nvidia and the US, and urged the board to rehire him. Reporting from Semafor now says that he was calling in to Nvidia’s board meeting around this time to make the same argument.

items.titleZh: 白宫吹嘘：特朗普“完全参与”促成詹森复职
items.descriptionZh:
这篇报道聚焦于特朗普政府公开介入英伟达CEO黄仁勋“复职”一事，核心不是技术发布，而是公司治理、国家安全审查与政治权力交叉的事件。文章称，黄仁勋此前因与一名被指为中国间谍的人有牵连而受到关注，引发对其是否构成国家安全风险的担忧；英伟达董事会随后决定恢复其CEO职位。白宫通讯主任史蒂文·张（Steven Cheung）向Semafor表示，特朗普“完全参与其中”，并称这是英伟达董事会的“伟大决定”，强调“我们必须保护我们的天才”。特朗普随后在CNBC上重复类似说法，称自己“非常强烈地相信”黄仁勋应复职，并表示政府进行了“非常彻底的调查”，调查显示黄仁勋在与一些“不太相关的事件”上判断不佳，但“没有做错任何事”。特朗普还称，如果他未介入，英伟达可能会在很长一段时间内处于“非常糟糕”的状态。

英伟达在公告中表示，董事会“收到了美国政府高级层级的意见”，这使其确信恢复黄仁勋职位不会构成国家安全风险。特朗普还在Truth Social上发文称，英伟达董事会做出了“正确且恰当的决定”，并称美国政府没有理由认为黄仁勋回归英伟达会对国家安全构成任何风险，美国司法部长已确认政府没有证据表明他从事任何非法行为。报道还称，在不到12小时前，特朗普曾在另一条帖子中表示，黄仁勋复职对英伟达和美国都是“最好的事情”，并敦促董事会重新聘用他；Semafor进一步报道称，特朗普当时还打电话进入英伟达董事会会议，提出同样的论点。

从背景看，这一事件发生在国家安全担忧与企业领导层稳定性交织的敏感时刻。英伟达作为AI芯片关键供应商，其CEO人选不仅影响公司战略和资本市场信心，也涉及美国政府对中国技术竞争、供应链安全和敏感人员关联的审查。文章中的“保护天才”说法，反映出特朗普政府将顶级科技企业领导者视为国家竞争力资产，并愿意通过公开表态甚至直接联系董事会来影响企业决策。其技术影响并不体现在芯片性能参数上，而体现在AI芯片龙头企业的治理独立性、政策风险管理以及美国政府与科技公司之间的关系上：如果政府高级层级的意见能够影响CEO复职决定，未来类似企业治理问题可能更频繁地被纳入国家安全和政治考量，进而影响英伟达的战略连续性、投资者预期以及AI芯片供应链的政策环境。

items.title: Russia readying nuclear-armed satellite that could destroy every low-Earth-orbit satellite, report claims
items.description: Intelligence agencies believe that Russia has spent the last several years readying Sputnik-S, a satellite armed with a nuclear weapon that could be used to destroy rival satellites in Earth's orbit — and it's expected to launch before the end of 2026.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Instagram Share this article 9 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Western intelligence agencies believe that Russia could be readying the launch of a nuclear-armed satellite before the end of the year. The satellite, called Sputnik-S, is believed to have been in development for the last several years, with the United States first warning of Russia's plans in February 2023. Now, a German news report believes that the country's armed forces are already "raising the alarm" about the potential impact such a satellite could have. According to one expert, such a weapon could knock out a third of low Earth orbit satellites instantly, eventually disabling all of them with a devastating impact on the planet as a whole. With satellites playing such a vital role for civilian life as well as both military and intelligence operations, it's easy to see why Russia may want such satellite-crippling capabilities.The report notes that information about Sputnik-S has been exchanged between several NATO member countries, with intelligence agencies having already warned that a launch could happen within 60 days. That report was made in early November, suggesting that Sputnik-S could be in orbit and operational in early December. The Russian embassy in Germany rejected the "unfounded allegations," saying that they are nothing more than "part of a propaganda campaign" against the country.Perhaps worryingly, the United States Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) published its own report in which it warned that "Russia is developing a satellite designed to carry a nuclear weapon." Such a move would be a violation of the 1967 Outer Space Treaty. The treaty prohibits any country from launching anything carrying nuclear weapons or, indeed, any weapon of mass destruction into Earth orbit. While there has been no suggestion that Russia could turn the nuclear weapons towards the planet, Sputnik-S would still clearly be in breach of the longstanding treaty. One expert cited by the report says that a nuclear explosion in space would knock out one-third of low Earth orbit satellites instantly, with the remaining satellites gradually failing in the following months. The EMP generated could even cause widespread technical carnage on Earth.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: As for which satellites could be a potential target for Sputnik-S, there is no shortage of options. SpaceX Starlink satellites are relied upon around the globe for their ability to provide fast, reliable networking to parts of the world not served by traditional connectivity options. Notably, Starlink has been used by Ukraine as it defends itself amid Russian aggression. But amid SpaceX's limiting of performance, Ukrainian officials have chosen to use their own "flying modems" to avoid relying on Elon Musk's company. Russia has been trying to launch its own Starlink rival, with limited success. September saw it lose a batch of 16 satellites during launch. items.titleZh: 报道称俄罗斯正筹备可摧毁所有近地轨道卫星的核武装卫星
items.descriptionZh:
西方情报机构认为，俄罗斯可能准备在年底前发射一颗名为“Sputnik-S”的核武装卫星。该卫星据信已研发数年，美国最早于2023年2月就俄罗斯的相关计划发出警告。德国媒体报道称，德国军方已就这颗卫星可能造成的影响“拉响警报”。有专家警告，这类武器可瞬间摧毁三分之一的地球低轨卫星，并在随后数月内使其余卫星逐渐失效，从而对全球造成灾难性影响。由于卫星在民用生活、军事行动和情报活动中都扮演关键角色，俄罗斯寻求这种瘫痪卫星的能力并不难理解。

报道指出，多个北约成员国之间已交换关于“Sputnik-S”的信息，情报机构警告发射可能在60天内发生。该报告发布于11月初，意味着“Sputnik-S”可能在12月初入轨并投入运行。俄罗斯驻德国大使馆否认相关指控，称这些是“毫无根据的指控”，只是针对俄罗斯的“宣传运动”的一部分。更令人担忧的是，美国国防情报局（DIA）也发布报告警告称，“俄罗斯正在开发一种设计用于携带核武器的卫星”。此举将违反1967年《外层空间条约》。该条约禁止任何国家将核武器或任何大规模毁灭性武器送入地球轨道。尽管目前没有迹象表明俄罗斯会把核武器对准地球，但“Sputnik-S”仍显然违反这一长期条约。

技术层面，专家指出，在太空实施核爆炸会瞬间摧毁三分之一的低轨卫星，剩余卫星将在随后数月内逐渐失效；核爆产生的电磁脉冲（EMP）甚至可能在地球上造成大范围技术灾难。其原理在于，高空核爆会释放强烈辐射和电磁脉冲，低轨卫星缺乏大气层屏蔽，电子系统容易受到辐射损伤和EMP耦合影响，导致通信、姿态控制、电源管理等关键子系统失效。潜在受影响目标很多。SpaceX的“星链”（Starlink）卫星在全球范围内为传统连接方式难以覆盖的地区提供快速可靠网络服务，乌克兰在抵御俄罗斯进攻过程中也使用了“星链”。不过，由于SpaceX限制性能，乌克兰官员已选择使用本国“飞行调制解调器”，以避免依赖埃隆·马斯克的公司。俄罗斯也在尝试发射自己的“星链”竞争对手，但进展有限，9月曾在发射中损失16颗卫星。

总体来看，“Sputnik-S”若投入使用，将不仅是军备控制层面的重大升级，也可能对低轨卫星生态、全球通信网络、军事指挥与情报体系以及民用基础设施产生连锁影响。其威胁重点并非核弹头直接打击地面，而是通过太空核爆产生的辐射与电磁脉冲效应，大面积瘫痪依赖低轨卫星的通信、侦察和网络服务。相关动向也凸显低轨卫星系统在军事与民用领域的战略价值，以及国际社会围绕太空武器化、卫星抗辐射加固和太空行为规范展开博弈的紧迫性。

items.title: AI server makers hike prices up to 45% months after contracts are signed as RAM shortage triples memory-heavy CPU node costs
items.description: AI server OEMs are hiking prices post-contract up to 45% — financial firms building datacenters still pay up as "the compute is valuable"
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Instagram Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter "Prices are really expensive for technology X" isn't truly news anymore, but it seems that even the bigshots who place orders in the magnitude of hundreds of millions of dollars are feeling the pinch. According to the Financial Times (FT), trading and financial service firms are seeing post-contract hikes of up to 45% on their data center servers.The price upgrades are coming in well after the ink has dried on the respective agreements, often signed months in advance. One unnamed person told the FT that "it is disconcerting when you get a 25, 30, 45 percent" increase, further adding that "there is a significant disparity" between the initial figure and the one that pops up on the final invoice.However, even this bump isn't deterring well-funded financial firms, which are reportedly buying up as much compute power as they can get their hands on, and are willing to eat the cost. Another informant said "we've never said no," noting that "at the end of the day, the compute is valuable to us and we'll pay for it." The FT asked whether the contacted companies had any clauses in their contracts preventing price volatility, but none confirmed or denied the fact.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The publication predictably points to RAM pricing as the main cause behind the out-of-nowhere hikes, noting that while GPU servers have risen in price by 20-30%, memory-heavy CPU nodes purportedly doubled or tripled in price.This is arguably more bad news for us peons, as it illustrates the DRAM shortage is alive and well, whether natural or fabricated. Furthermore, it shows if even the big shots are more than willing to pay inflated prices, then mere mortals have little chance of a RAM price reprieve. You may like Apple faces unprecedented memory cost increases as RAM prices continue to surge, manufacturing bill climbs by $33 billion DDR5 laptop memory prices surge 6X in 12 months AI-induced memory shortage is changing how devices are built, Fairphone says memory now 60% of materials cost Not every firm is taking the price jacking lying down, though. Back in June, XTX Finland Oy took one of Dell's Irish subsidiaries to court, after Dell asked for another $62 to $70 million on top of the previously agreed-on price of $549 million for 1,680 servers. That case is still ongoing and is an interesting watch, as XTX apparently paid $5 million extra for a contract clause specifically to prevent any pricing shenanigans.Even if XTX wins, though, the firm may find it harder to do future business with OEMs. The supply-demand balance is currently so lopsided that chip fabs and OEMs have all the ability to pretty much set any terms they wish.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors Download the Tom's Hardware app for up-to-the-minute updates on iOS and Android. items.titleZh: AI服务器厂商签约数月后涨价高达45%，内存短缺令内存密集型CPU节点成本增至三倍
items.descriptionZh:
据《金融时报》报道，交易和金融服务公司在数据中心服务器采购中正遭遇合同签署后的追加涨价，涨幅最高达45%。这类合同通常提前数月签订，但最终发票金额较最初约定显著上升。一位匿名人士称，25%、30%甚至45%的涨幅“令人不安”，初始报价与最终账单之间存在“巨大差异”。即便如此，资金雄厚的金融公司仍在大举抢购算力，并愿意承担涨价成本。另一名知情人士表示“我们从未说过不”，因为“归根结底，算力对我们有价值，我们会付钱”。FT询问相关公司合同中是否有防止价格波动的条款，但未得到确认或否认。

报道将涨价主因指向内存（RAM）价格飙升。GPU服务器价格上涨约20%至30%，而内存密集型CPU节点价格据称翻倍甚至涨至三倍。这反映出DRAM短缺仍在持续，无论其成因是自然供需还是人为因素。服务器成本结构上，GPU服务器依赖GPU及高带宽内存，而内存密集型CPU节点对大容量DRAM更敏感，因此在本轮内存涨价中受冲击更大。对金融交易和金融服务场景而言，低延迟、高吞吐的算力直接关系到交易执行、实时风控和数据分析能力，这也是相关企业即便面对合同后加价仍不愿退出采购的原因。文章还指出，如果连下百亿美元级订单的大型机构都愿意接受虚高价格，普通消费者短期内更难看到内存价格回落。

并非所有公司都默默接受涨价。今年6月，XTX Finland Oy将戴尔一家爱尔兰子公司告上法庭。戴尔此前已同意以5.49亿美元向XTX供应1680台服务器，随后又要求追加6200万至7000万美元。该案仍在审理中。值得注意的是，XTX据称曾额外支付500万美元，专门加入防止价格变动的合同条款。不过，即使XTX胜诉，未来与原始设备制造商（OEM）做生意也可能更困难。当前供需失衡严重偏向供给方，芯片晶圆厂和OEM几乎有能力设定任何他们想要的条款，服务器采购方在价格谈判中的议价空间被明显压缩。
